unresolved_should_improve.claim: Both drafts say the Trent Affair ended the idea of being useful, then tell only the Manchester/Times satire story. They omit the source's explanation that 'The Trent Affair dwarfed individual effort.' The satire episode therefore reads as if the Trent Affair caused it, or the stated link is never justified.
unresolved_should_improve.counterevidence: The Times episode alone partly motivates the renunciation of zeal.

evidence.quote: The Trent Affair dwarfed individual effort.
The Trent Affair had one result personal to him: to put an end forever to the idea of being "useful."
Henry Adams escaped, but he never tried to be useful again. "Surtout point de zele!"

unresolved_should_improve.minimal_repair: Insert 'The Trent Affair dwarfed individual effort.' before 'Surtout point de zele!'
unresolved_should_improve.plan_relation: required (Times satire and the end of 'usefulness' are essential)
unresolved_should_improve.reader_effect: The causal claim floats. Readers may misconnect the satire with the Trent crisis rather than see the crisis as dwarfing all personal zeal.
unresolved_should_improve.title: Trent Affair's role in ending 'usefulness' is left unexplained

unresolved_should_improve.claim: The revision cuts 'They were glad to face the end' and the reasoning that, since England meant to strike, they were eager to strike first. It keeps only the bare 'They saw it and cheered it!'
unresolved_should_improve.counterevidence: 'Nervous as wild beasts under the long strain' survives and partly explains the outburst.

evidence.quote: They were glad to face the end.
Since England was waiting only for its own moment to strike, they were eager to strike first.
broke into shouts of delight. They saw it and cheered it!

unresolved_should_improve.minimal_repair: Restore the final sentence: 'Since England was waiting only for its own moment to strike, they were eager to strike first.'
unresolved_should_improve.plan_relation: required (Trent news cheered by the secretaries as war)
unresolved_should_improve.reader_effect: The secretaries' delight at war loses its logic of relief and pre-emption, and the paradox reads as mere hysteria.
unresolved_should_improve.title: Motive for cheering a declaration of war removed

unresolved_should_improve.claim: The source explains the luck: with a palace and a trained staff he would still be cabin-boy, with many masters. The revision cuts this hypothetical, so 'Luckily... he was alone' jumps straight to 'most fortunate person'.
unresolved_should_improve.counterevidence: 'having for master only his father' still implies the contrast.

evidence.quote: still, with the extra burden of many masters; he was the most fortunate
Had he been given a palace in London and a staff of trained secretaries, he would have been cabin-boy still
Luckily for the cabin-boy, he was alone. He was the most fortunate person in the party

unresolved_should_improve.minimal_repair: Restore a clause: 'Had the Minister been given a palace and a staff of trained secretaries, the private secretary would have been cabin-boy still, with the extra burden of many masters;'
unresolved_should_improve.plan_relation: required (V2 sets up the recurring cabin-boy image)
unresolved_should_improve.reader_effect: A characteristic ironic reversal becomes an unexplained assertion, and the cabin-boy image (V2) is less developed.
unresolved_should_improve.title: Cabin-boy 'luckily alone' joke loses its premise

unresolved_should_improve.claim: The revision cuts the source's case that the Minister's consent to leave a safe Congressional seat for London, with only Sumner's doubtful support, was the weakest proof of his fitness. 'Never before had they taken one so desperate' now follows only the joke about the secretary's unfitness.
unresolved_should_improve.counterevidence: Para 4's 'no friend in the Senate' partly recovers the danger later.

evidence.quote: his consent to quit a safe seat in Congress for an exceedingly unsafe seat in London
the weakest of all Mr. Adams's proofs of fitness was his consent to quit a safe seat in Congress
In the family history, its members had taken many a dangerous risk, but never before had they taken one so desperate.

unresolved_should_improve.minimal_repair: Restore a short clause before the final sentence: 'the weakest proof of his fitness was his consent to quit a safe seat in Congress for an exceedingly unsafe seat in London.'
unresolved_should_improve.plan_relation: optional tradeoff not listed; this is a planning omission of a hinge
unresolved_should_improve.reader_effect: This loses the ironic Sumner jab and the concrete reason the family risk was desperate. The closing sentence of the paragraph becomes vague.
unresolved_should_improve.title: 'So desperate' risk detached from its ground
